cards.pronunciationNote: Formal greeting used until ~6 PM
cards.exampleSentence: Guten Tag, wie geht es Ihnen?
cards.exampleTranslation: Good day, how are you? | শুভ দিন, আপনি কেমন আছেন?
cards.grammarTip: Use 'guten Tag' formally. Informal: 'Hallo' or 'Tag'

cards.pronunciationNote: Informal, universal greeting
cards.exampleTranslation: Hello! I am Anna. | হ্যালো! আমি আনা।
cards.grammarTip: Used with friends, family, and peers (du-form)

cards.pronunciationNote: Informal goodbye, pronounced like 'chüss'
cards.exampleTranslation: Bye, see you soon! | বায়, শীঘ্রই দেখা হবে!
cards.grammarTip: Casual goodbye. Formal: 'Auf Wiedersehen'

cards.pronunciationNote: Universal thank you
cards.exampleTranslation: Thank you very much! | খুব ধন্যবাদ!
cards.grammarTip: 'Danke schön' is more polite. Response: 'Bitte schön'

cards.pronunciationNote: Means both 'please' and 'you're welcome'
cards.exampleTranslation: A coffee, please. | একটা কফি, দয়া করে।
cards.grammarTip: As 'please': at end of request. As 'welcome': response to 'danke'

cards.pronunciationNote: Pronounced 'ikh' (ich-laut), not 'ish'
cards.exampleTranslation: My name is Maria. | আমার নাম মারিয়া।
cards.grammarTip: Always lowercase unless at sentence start. Verb conjugation: ich + -e

cards.pronunciationNote: Regular verb: ich komme, du kommst, er kommt
cards.exampleTranslation: I come from Germany. | আমি জার্মানি থেকে এসেছি।
cards.grammarTip: Use 'aus' + dative for origin: aus Deutschland, aus Bangladesch

cards.pronunciationNote: Regular verb: ich wohne, du wohnst, er wohnt
cards.exampleTranslation: I live in Berlin. | আমি বারলিনে থাকি।
cards.grammarTip: Use 'in' + dative for cities/countries: in Berlin, in Deutschland

cards.pronunciationNote: heesen
cards.exampleSentence: Wie heißen Sie? Ich heiße Thomas.
cards.exampleTranslation: What is your name? My name is Thomas. | আপনার নাম কি? আমার নাম থমাস।
cards.grammarTip: Formal: 'Wie heißen Sie?' Informal: 'Wie heißt du?'

cards.pronunciationNote: Irregular verb: ich bin, du bist, er ist, wir sind, ihr seid, sie sind
cards.exampleTranslation: I am a student. | আমি একজন ছাত্র।
cards.grammarTip: Most irregular verb. Memorize all forms: bin, bist, ist, sind, seid, sind

cards.pronunciationNote: Irregular: ich habe, du hast, er hat, wir haben, ihr habt, sie haben
cards.exampleTranslation: I have a car. | আমার একটা গাড়ি আছে।
cards.grammarTip: Use 'haben' for possession. Akkusativ: ich habe EINEN Bruder

cards.pronunciationNote: Vowel change: ich spreche, du sprichst, er spricht (e→ie)
cards.exampleTranslation: Do you speak German? | আপনি কি জার্মান বলেন?
cards.grammarTip: Stem-changing verb (e→ie). Formal: Sprechen Sie? Informal: Sprichst du?

cards.pronunciationNote: Regular verb: ich verstehe, du verstehst, er versteht
cards.exampleTranslation: I don't understand. | আমি বুঝি না।
cards.grammarTip: Negation with 'nicht' at end: Ich verstehe NICHT

cards.pronunciationNote: Regular verb: ich lerne, du lernst, er lernt
cards.exampleTranslation: I learn German. | আমি জার্মান শিখছি।
cards.grammarTip: Regular verb pattern. Add -e, -st, -t, -en, -t, -en to stem 'lern-'

cards.pronunciationNote: Add 'e' before endings: ich arbeite, du arbeitest, er arbeitet
cards.exampleTranslation: I work in a company. | আমি একটা কোম্পানিতে কাজ করি।
cards.grammarTip: Verbs ending in -t/-d add 'e': arbeiten → du arbeitest, er arbeitet

cards.pronunciationNote: Masculine: der Vorname, plural: die Vornamen
cards.exampleTranslation: My first name is Hans. | আমার প্রথম নাম হ্যান্স।
cards.grammarTip: Compound: VOR (before) + NAME. Always masculine: DER Vorname

cards.pronunciationNote: Masculine: der Nachname, plural: die Nachnamen
cards.exampleTranslation: My last name is Müller. | আমার উপনাম মুলার।
cards.grammarTip: Compound: NACH (after) + NAME. Opposite of Vorname

cards.pronunciationNote: Feminine: die Sprache, plural: die Sprachen
cards.exampleTranslation: German is a beautiful language. | জার্মান একটা সুন্দর ভাষা।
cards.grammarTip: Ends in -e → usually feminine (die). Plural: -n (Sprachen)

cards.pronunciationNote: Neuter: das Wort, plural: die Wörter (umlaut ö)
cards.exampleTranslation: The word is new. | শব্দটা নতুন।
cards.grammarTip: Neuter nouns often don't have obvious endings. Plural: Wörter (umlaut!)

cards.pronunciationNote: Masculine: der Buchstabe, plural: die Buchstaben
cards.exampleTranslation: Please spell it. | দয়া করে স্পেল করুন।
cards.grammarTip: Compound: BUCH (book) + STABE (staff/letter). Masculine

cards.pronunciationNote: Adjective/adverb: 'langsam' (slow/slowly)
cards.exampleTranslation: Please speak slowly. | দয়া করে ধীরে বলুন।
cards.grammarTip: Adverbs don't change form. Same for adjective: ein langsames Auto

cards.pronunciationNote: Used until ~10 AM. Accusative: guten (masc.)
cards.exampleSentence: Guten Morgen! Wie geht es dir?
cards.exampleTranslation: Good morning! How are you? | সুপ্রভাত! তুমি কেমন আছো?
cards.grammarTip: Morgen is masculine → guten Morgen (accusative). Informal: Morgen!

cards.pronunciationNote: Used from ~6 PM. Accusative: guten (masc.)
cards.exampleTranslation: Good evening everyone! | শুভ সন্ধ্যা সবাইকে!
cards.grammarTip: Abend is masculine → guten Abend. Informal: 'n Abend!

cards.pronunciationNote: Only when going to sleep. Accusative: gute (fem.)
cards.exampleTranslation: Good night, sleep well! | শুভ রাত, ভালো ঘুমাও!
cards.grammarTip: Nacht is feminine → gute Nacht. Only for bedtime!

cards.pronunciationNote: Formal goodbye. Literally: 'until seeing again'
cards.exampleTranslation: Goodbye, Mr. Müller! | বিদায়, হের মুলার!
cards.grammarTip: Formal. Informal: 'Tschüs' or 'Bis bald'

cards.pronunciationNote: Masculine: der Herr, plural: die Herren
cards.exampleTranslation: Good day, Doctor. | শুভ দিন, ডাক্তার সাহেব।
cards.grammarTip: Title before last name: Herr Müller. Plural: die Herren (irregular)

cards.pronunciationNote: Feminine: die Frau, plural: die Frauen (umlaut ä)
cards.exampleTranslation: Mrs. Schmidt is a teacher. | শ্রীমতী שמিড্ট একটা শিক্ষক।
cards.grammarTip: Title before last name: Frau Schmidt. Plural: Frauen (umlaut!)

cards.pronunciationNote: Possessive article: mein (masc./neut.), meine (fem./plural)
cards.exampleTranslation: This is my book. | এটা আমার বই।
cards.grammarTip: Mein + masculine/neuter noun. Meine + feminine/plural noun

cards.pronunciationNote: Question word: 'where from' (wo + her)
cards.exampleTranslation: Where are you from? | আপনি কোথা থেকে আসছেন?
cards.grammarTip: Answer with 'aus' + dative: Ich komme aus Bangladesch

cards.pronunciationNote: Neuter country name, no article: IN Deutschland
cards.exampleTranslation: I come from Germany. | আমি জার্মানি থেকে এসেছি।
cards.grammarTip: Countries: usually neuter, no article. Aus DEUTSCHLAND (dative)

cards.pronunciationNote: Feminine: die Person, plural: die Personen
cards.exampleTranslation: She is a nice person. | সে একটা ভালো মানুষ।
cards.grammarTip: Ends in -on → feminine (die). From Latin. Plural: -en

quizQuestions.explanationBn: Bahnhof = train station. Masculine nouns: der Bahnhof. Most transport nouns are masculine.
Sprache = language. Ends in -e → usually feminine (die Sprache). Plural: die Sprachen.
Ich + verb stem + e = ich komme. Regular verb conjugation for 'ich'.
Du + verb stem + st = du sprichst. Stem change e→ie: sprechen → sprichst.

quizQuestions.promptText: Listen and select the correct number
quizQuestions.explanationBn: siebenundzwanzig = 27 (sieben + und + zwanzig). German numbers: unit + und + tens.

quizQuestions.promptText: Listen and select the correct time
quizQuestions.explanationBn: Halb neun = half to nine = 8:30. German 'halb' refers to the COMING hour.
Mädchen = girl. Ends in -chen → ALWAYS neuter (das Mädchen), even for people!
Yes/No question: verb first! Kommst du...? (verb + subject). Statement: Du kommst...
Buch is neuter (das Buch) → mein (no ending). Feminine/plural would be 'meine'.
Akkusativ masculine: der → DEN. Ich sehe DEN Mann (direct object).

quizQuestions.promptText: Modal verb: Ich ______ nach Hause gehen. (wollen)
quizQuestions.explanationBn: ich will (irregular modal). Modal at position 2, infinitive 'gehen' at END.
Perfekt with haben: ich HABE gearbeitet. Most verbs use haben. Motion verbs use sein.
